name: Permanent Resident Visa / Quota Immigrant Visa (Section 13)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a slot within the annual Section 13 immigration quota, historically set at a small fixed number per nationality per year under the Philippine Immigration Act of 1940.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm current quota availability for the applicable nationality directly with the Bureau of Immigration.

requirements.blocker_text: For former Filipino citizens (who have not reacquired citizenship under RA 9225) returning to reside permanently in the Philippines.
requirements.fix_path: Consider ph_ra9225_dual_citizenship instead if seeking to reacquire citizenship rather than only permanent-resident status.

requirements.blocker_text: For individuals who previously held Philippine permanent resident status and are returning after a period abroad.

evidence_required.document: Category-specific documentation (quota confirmation, former-citizenship proof, or prior PR status proof)

sources.title: VisaFoto -- Philippines Visa Guide for 2026, listing the Section 13 immigrant-visa subcategories (13(a) marriage, 13(e) returning resident, 13(g) returning former citizen, plain 13 quota)

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a Bureau of Immigration page confirming current Section 13 quota numbers per nationality was achieved in this research pass -- the Quota Immigrant Visa's practical availability varies significantly by nationality and the specific current allocation was not confirmed. STRUCTURAL FINDING: 'Section 13' functions as an umbrella covering several genuinely distinct immigrant-visa subcategories with different qualifying logic -- this file models the plain quota category plus the two 'returning' categories (13(e) and 13(g)), while 13(a) marriage-based immigration is deliberately modeled as its own separate route file (ph_marriage_visa_13a) given how much distinctive detail (reciprocity gating, probationary conversion) that specific subcategory carries. 13(g) is explicitly distinct from and can be used instead of ph_ra9225_dual_citizenship for a former Filipino who wants only permanent-resident status without reacquiring full citizenship -- a real choice point for former Filipinos worth surfacing, since the two routes lead to meaningfully different end states (resident alien vs. citizen) despite serving an overlapping population.
